questions.stem: Why is a transit a particularly good line of position?
options: It needs no charted objects at all
It is always a fix on its own
Compass-free, and exact if well charted
It is only useful at night
questions.explanation: Two objects in line define a straight line on the chart, so no compass reading is involved. Crossed with another line, it gives a fix.

questions.stem: What does a clearing bearing labelled NMT mean?
options: Bearing must not exceed it; danger side hatched
The ship must keep the bearing exactly at the stated value
The mark must bear at least the stated value
The hatched side is the safe side
questions.explanation: NMT is 'not more than'. The danger side is hatched so that it is clear which side to avoid. NLT is 'not less than'.

questions.stem: When drawing a clearing line past a reef, where should the line be placed?
options: Exactly through the edge of the reef
Through the middle of the reef
Clear of the reef, with a margin
On the far side of the reef from the ship
questions.explanation: A clearing line is a limit, so it should leave a margin between the line and the danger. A line touching the danger gives no allowance for error.

questions.stem: You steer on a leading line of two beacons. The front beacon appears to the left of the rear beacon. What does this tell you?
options: The ship is exactly on the line
The beacons are misidentified on the chart
The compass error has changed
She is off the line; it shows which way
questions.explanation: When the front mark opens from the rear mark the ship has left the line. The sense of the opening tells you which way to come back.

questions.stem: A true clearing bearing of the light is NLT 038 degrees. The ship's compass error on the present heading is 14 degrees E. What is the limit in compass terms?
options: NLT 052 degrees by compass
NMT 024 degrees by compass
NLT 024 degrees by compass
NLT 038 degrees by compass
questions.explanation: True to compass: subtract easterly error, 038 - 14 = 024. The sense NLT is unchanged. 052 uses the wrong sign, and 038 forgets to convert.

questions.stem: A ship approaches a light on a track of 045 degrees. A reef lies to starboard of the track. If she drifts toward the reef, the light moves toward her port bow. Which clearing bearing is correct?
options: NLT: not less than a stated bearing
NMT: not more than a stated bearing
The bearing must be exactly 045 degrees
No clearing bearing is possible here
questions.explanation: Drifting to starboard makes the light bear less (it moves toward the port bow), so the safe condition stops the bearing from decreasing: NLT. Always ask which way the bearing changes as the ship moves toward the danger.

questions.stem: Which object is the best mark for a clearing bearing or transit?
options: A floating buoy near the danger
An unidentified rock awash
A moored vessel nearby
A fixed, charted light or beacon
questions.explanation: Fixed objects stay where the chart says. A buoy may be off station and cannot guarantee that you are clear of a danger.

questions.stem: After an alteration of course, what should be done with a clearing bearing converted to compass?
options: Keep using the old compass figure
Apply the old compass error to a hand compass
Redo it with the new heading's error
Cancel the clearing bearing altogether
questions.explanation: The true limit stays the same. The compass limit depends on the deviation for the heading, which changes when the heading changes.

options: Two transits that cross
A single transit
A single clearing bearing
A depth contour alone
questions.explanation: Each transit is a line of position. Two lines that cross, or a transit and a bearing or range, give a fix. A clearing bearing is a limit, not a fix.

questions.stem: How do you hatch a clearing bearing on the chart?
options: On the safe side of the line
On both sides of the line
Along the track, ahead of the ship
On the danger side
questions.explanation: Hatching marks the side you must keep out of, so anyone reading the plot knows at a glance.
